business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Portable Phased-Array Medical Diagnostic Scanners

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law in Quebec private matters; Federal Common Law for public and criminal matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU
Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1 (register of individuals with significant control and UBO obligations); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; associated PCMLTFA regulations, SOR/2002-184.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of each UBO and director passport bio-page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office / notary public in country of citizenship

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / certificate of conduct for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national police or criminal-records authority of country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / incumbency for any corporate shareholder acting as UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of companies of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing Quebec legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / corporate director acting as principal

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List; (iii) Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act; and (iv) relevant international financial sanctions under the United Nations Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. Politically exposed persons (PEP) determination, including family members and close associates, must follow FINTRAC guidance and PCMLTFA risk-based due-diligence requirements, with enhanced monitoring where applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises (Quebec Enterprise Register / REQ Online)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) mandates that enterprise names be expressed in French. A non-French distinctive part is allowed only when accompanied by a French generic term or a registered trademark, and foreign-script characters must be transliterated into Latin script. The French form must be used in all public registrants and for any pre-incorporation name-clearance filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a name-rejection notice, the filer may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. If rejection is confirmed, an application for review may be filed before the Tribunal administratif du Québec within 30 days of the confirmation, under the applicable rules of procedure. No extension of the 120-day reservation is available; the proposer must submit a new name reservation after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permitted only if it provides a physical address in Quebec where process can be formally served and from which corporate records can be produced. It does not, however, satisfy the commercial-substance and facility requirements applicable to a Health Canada licensed medical-device establishment; for a manufacturing/export business, a dedicated physical facility in Quebec is required for the statutory licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 75% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection for a Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence holder under the Medical Devices Regulations SOR/98-282, given the manufacturing and importing scope.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory name reservation and clearance search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (Registraire des entreprises fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of Incorporation filing fee under the Quebec Business Corporations Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (Registraire des entreprises fee schedule)

Notarization and Hague Apostille / consular legalization of identity and authority bundles
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary and Global Affairs Canada / Quebec competent authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation regulatory assessment of Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence requirements
Destination-country consular legalization of export certificates (optional, buyer-specific)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1, Part II (ss. 3-23) and Part VII (registered office, ss. 115-127; by-laws, ss. 128-133)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) and declaration of individual response
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; incorporation may be completed with nil paid-up capital. Shares must be issued for consideration adequate in the directors’ judgment; no escrow account is required by statute, but the share register must record actual subscriptions and any bank account opening will require the financial institution’s minimum deposit under KYC/AML rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The share subscription schedule presented by the incorporators is approved; the Board authorizes issuance of one Class A common share for each dollar of subscription paid, and no escrow restriction applies. 2. The registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [Address], City of [City], Province of Quebec, and the Chief Executive Officer is appointed keeper of the corporate records. 3. The officers of the Corporation are appointed to serve until the next annual general meeting: [Name], Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Secretary–Treasurer; [Name], Chief Financial Officer. 4. Management is authorized to open bank accounts, negotiate trade financing, and execute all filings required for industrial licensing and environmental assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Name Portal (https://www.registraire.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a pre-search in the Registraire’s corporate name database; assess distinctiveness and prohibition under s. 14 QBCA; confirm the French wording is available; optionally reserve the name for 90 days through the online service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, modify the distinctive element or use a numbered company; resubmit the name reservation within 30 days; no monetary penalty if corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal drafting by incorporator/counsel; no prior governmental clearance required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Quebec BCA Articles of Incorporation containing share structure, share rights, transfer restrictions (if any), number of directors, registered office address and French-language texts. Draft By-Law No. 1 and the organizational consent forms. Ensure the French version is complete and certified in accordance with the Charter of the French Language.
required_dossiers: Written consent of incorporator and first directors
French language certificate or complete French version
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If drafting is queried, amend the articles by supplemental resolution or file an application for rectification under Part XIV QBCA; cure linguistic insufficiency by a certified translation before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online filing gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Articles of Incorporation and supporting declaration online; pay the registration fee; the REQ issues an electronic certificate and assigns a Numéro d’entreprise du Québec (NEQ) upon constitution. Verify legal ending “Inc.” or “Corp.” and registered office address.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation in electronic file
Declaration of incorporation and registered office
Identification and consent of first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a query, respond within 15 calendar days with corrected wording or notice of error; if certificate is defective, apply for a certificate of correction under s. 119 QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organizational Meeting and Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Revenu Québec; banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting: adopt the first board resolution, approve share issuance, fix registered office, appoint officers, approve banking resolution and financial signatory authority. Register the corporation with CRA for Business Number, GST/HST and payroll; register with Revenu Québec for QST and source deductions; open the corporate bank account and deposit subscribed capital.
required_dossiers: Director/officer identification and social insurance numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA/Revenu Québec rejects registration due to mismatch, correct the NEQ records through REQ and resubmit; dispute any tax registration refusal by notice within 90 days under the Tax Administration Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Premises and Occupational Licensing Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal building and fire services; Commission des normes, de l’équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST); Health Canada – Medical Devices Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Inspect and certify the manufacturing site as compliant with municipal zoning for NAICS 334510; obtain an occupancy permit and fire safety certificate; register as an employer with CNESST; compile and submit the Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence application (together with device-class and ISO certification, if applicable) for the colour Doppler ultrasound console.
required_dossiers: Lease or title to the facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If occupancy or fire clearance is refused, carry out corrective works and obtain re-inspection; a denial by CNESST may be appealed to the Administrative Labour Court; Health Canada deficiencies are cured by updated additional information requests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada – Medical Devices Directorate (MDD); Quebec Ministère de l’Économie, de l’Innovation et de l’Énergie (MEIE); Municipal building and fire departments
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) and, as applicable, Medical Device Licence (MDL) for the Class II colour Doppler ultrasound console; CNESST occupational safety acceptance; municipal occupancy permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt (Category C): no full EIA required for low-volume electronic assembly; mandatory sectoral authorization if the plant’s solvent use, wastewater flow, or VOCs exceed the thresholds of the Québec environmental quality regulation (REAFIE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater: pH 6–9.5, BOD5 ≤300 mg/L, TSS ≤350 mg/L, and compliance with municipal sewer by-law and s. 22 Environment Quality Act if a discharge to a watercourse is proposed. VOC: aggregate solvent emissions must be reported if above 10 t/yr and require certificate of authorization above 30 t/yr. Hazardous waste: storage below 1 t/month without a waste plan; manifests and transport approvals under Regulation respecting hazardous materials (CQLR c Q-2, r. 32) for electronic boards, solder flux, batteries and transducer reagents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety certificate and regular inspection; structural load certificate by a Québec engineer for the production floor under Chapter I of the Québec Construction Code; CNESST clearance for electrical hazard, noise, VOCs and machine guarding; compliance with Canadian Electrical Code Part I and CSA C22.2 No. 60601-1 for medical electrical equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — portal: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency; in Quebec, Revenu Québec (portal: revenu.quebec.ca) administers GST/HST and QST collection under a single tax administration agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Canadian/Quebec operating presence must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 or through the online Business Registration Online (BRO) service. The BN is mandatory for GST/HST and QST registration. For QST, the entity must also register with Revenu Québec, obtaining a Quebec Business Number (NEQ) and a QST registration number. Non-resident registrants must appoint a Canadian resident agent for service where required. The SOP: (1) incorporate or otherwise obtain a legal presence; (2) complete RC1/BRO application; (3) provide evidence of foreign registration, director/officer identities, and Canadian place of business; (4) receive BN and GST/HST/QST accounts; (5) file registration notice and comply with provincial attestations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — Canadian business corporations are taxed as separate taxpayers at the federal and provincial levels; no flow-through classification available for Inc./Corp. structure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists under the Canadian Income Tax Act; classification follows legal form. Relevant statutory elections include s.85 rollover elections, s.97(2) partnership rollovers, s.256 amalgamation elections, s.211 wind-up elections, and s.219 deemed dividend elections for non-resident corporations. Hybrid mismatch rules introduced in 2022 require self-review and disallowance/structuring elections under Part XII.6; no elective avoidance is permitted, but limited structuring elections exist for certain structured arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in the current or immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST and QST small supplier threshold; non-residents carrying on business in Canada (including Quebec) are subject to the same threshold and mandatory registration once exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or pre-clearance electronic invoicing regime. Tax invoices must meet prescribed GST/HST invoice content (Excise Tax Act s.169/223; QST under the QSST Act). Digital invoices are permitted; voluntary secure electronic invoicing standards (e.g., Peppol BIS) are available. No digital stamping or API-based fiscal authorization applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, exports of goods are zero-rated (0% GST/HST) if shipped out of Canada by the supplier or delivered to a common carrier for export, and the exporter retains proof of export documentation. Services are zero-rated if supplied to a non-resident of Canada, unless the service relates to real property in Canada, tangible personal property normally used in Canada, or certain domestic elements. QST zero-rating follows equivalent rules pursuant to the QSST Act for export supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Business Number and GST/HST registration number
Bill of lading / air waybill or other shipping documentation
CBSA B13A Export Declaration (or Canadian Export Reporting System electronic record)
Customs-powered evidence of physical movement: highway export reporting, carrier Cargo Control Document, terminal receipts
Inward remittance certificate / bank transfer confirmation of payment for exported goods (where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rated claims retroactively for up to 4 years (7 years for misrepresentation/fraud) and deny zero-rating where proof-of-export documentation is incomplete. Penalties include: gross negligence penalty under Excise Tax Act s.285.1 (equal to 10% of tax assessed or $200, whichever greater), false statements or omissions under s.281.1, interest on net tax, and potential criminal prosecution under s.327 of the ETA / Criminal Code for fraudulent manipulation. Revenu Québec may similarly impose fines under the QSST Act and retain QST rebates. Retrospective clawback of input tax credits (ITCs) and QST refunds generally accompanies denial of zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central bank responsible for issuing Canadian bank notes and overseeing the national payments system. Canada does not maintain a centralized foreign exchange control authority; the regulatory perimeter is as follows: the Department of Finance sets currency and exchange policy under the Currency Act; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions supervises federally regulated banks; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada enforces AML/KYC obligations; and the Bank of Canada operates the Large Value Transfer System for wholesale clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is a full convertibility jurisdiction. Both current and capital account transactions are broadly unrestricted: there is no general exchange control legislation, no obligatory central bank approval for foreign direct investment, and no pre-approval requirement for dividend remittances or profit repatriation. Remittances are subject only to Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (typically 25% statute rate, subject to treaty relief), and certain reporting requirements under the Canadian Payments Act, OFSI/Statistics Canada surveys, and the International Transactions Reporting System. Therefore, the Color Doppler Ultrasound Console manufacturing entity may freely convert CAD to USD/EUR/CNY, maintain foreign currency bank accounts, and repatriate profits through standard cleared bank wires without Canadian exchange control authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds surrender. Exporters are permitted to retain export earnings in foreign currency bank accounts, invoice in foreign currency, and sell foreign currency through Canadian Authorized Financial Institutions at market rates. There is no legal obligation to repatriate export proceeds within a prescribed period; however, for tax and financial reporting purposes, export receipts must be recognized in accordance with Canadian GAAP/IFRS and the Income Tax Act, and each cross-border wire must comply with the Bank of Canada's clearing standards, FINTRAC 24-hour reporting thresholds, and DPR/ITRS reporting where applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low for an offshore digital EMI to act as a primary corporate bank in Canada; Medium only if such EMI obtains FINTRAC MSB registration and obtains a Canadian banking agent/partner for domestic CAD clearing. Under the Bank Act and the Payment Clearing and Settlement Act, an offshore EMI cannot accept deposits or open a Canadian clearing account in its own name without being a Schedule I bank or otherwise obtaining Canadian regulatory authorization. For the Color Doppler Ultrasound Console exporter, offshore digital EMIs should be used solely as non-bank FX/remittance auxiliary channels, never as the main treasury clearing rail, to avoid AML and deposit-taking infringement risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no blanket Canadian statutory mandate requiring every director to appear physically for corporate account opening. Federally regulated banks, however, operate under PCMLTFA/AML directives and their own risk appetite, which almost always require either in-person verification of the account signatories/beneficial owners or remote video verification supplemented by certified true copies, apostilled board resolutions, and notarized passports. For a Quebec-based corp, the practical standard is: Chair/CFO and any authorized signatory should appear in person at the account-opening branch; other directors may satisfy KYC remotely through high-assurance digital verification. A purely remote process is possible for Low-Risk Standard medical-device exporters only when the bank's onboarding platform supports video KYC and the ownership structure is fully transparent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative news, PEP status, or sanctions-list hit on a director/beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full biographical summaries, employment references, declaration of non-PEP or PEP explanation, certified passport and proof of residential address for each director, and an independent legal opinion confirming no sanctioned ownership, plus a FINTRAC-compliant risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregate beneficial ownership is opaque or scattered through foreign holdings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate registry extract showing all registered shareholders, an updated Canadian federal/Quebec register of individuals with significant control (ISC), translated and apostilled ownership deeds/trust declarations, and a source-of-wealth breakdown for each shareholder holding more than 10%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a FATF-grey-listed or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business rationale and transaction flowchart, signed investment agreement, pro-forma invoices/purchase orders, bank references from the sending institution, evidence of tax residence, and a legal forensic source-of-funds opinion prepared by a Canadian counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected early drawdown of escrowed capital or high-volume outbound wires to new vendors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow release conditions, board-approved treasury policy, board resolutions authorizing trade settlement limits, corresponding SWIFT MT103 payment messages, supplier due diligence files, and annual audited financial statements or audited capital utilization report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via SWIFT or Fedwire/CHIPS into the Canadian corporate account using standard purpose codes and remittance narratives. Capital injections should be designated as unaudited share capital or shareholder loan with SWIFT purpose code 'EQUI' or 'INTE' where supported, plus a clear remittance message such as 'SC-EQUI / subscription price paid into Canadian operating entity'. For amounts exceeding CAD 10,000, the receiving bank must be supplied with the corporate KYC pack and the board resolution authorizing the account; Statistics Canada's International Investment Position reporting threshold is triggered by direct investment; the funds must be booked as contributed surplus or share capital in the financial statements. A capital verification certificate issued by the Quebec business register is not required for incorporation but should be prepared for the bank's escrow release evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements will be executed through the Canadian banking system using SWIFT MT103 for open-account TT wires and commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 (MT700/MT707) for documentary trade. CAD-denominated domestic flows clear through the Bank of Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS), USD flows clear through Fedwire/CHIPS, and EUR/CNY flows clear through correspondent banks at major Canadian clearing institutions. Outbound payments must include full invoice number, pro-forma invoice reference, commodity description for medical ultrasound consoles, and relevant HS/ECC codes. To mitigate stranded liquidity, a multicurrency account or specialized USD/EUR/CNY sub-account should be held with the same Canadian Schedule I bank to permit automatic sweep and netting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts (CAD vs USD, CAD vs EUR, CAD vs CNY)
Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) for restricted or thinly traded currencies (e.g., INR, KRW, and other non-convertible jurisdictions)
Cross-currency swap agreements (FX swaps) for treasury liquidity position management
Franked plain-vanilla FX options (calls/puts) with trade underlying documentation
Money market hedging through foreign currency demand/time deposits at Canadian Schedule I banks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of federal incorporation (not fiscal year-end); filed online through the Corporations Canada portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continued non-filing permits administrative dissolution by the Director after one to two years of missed returns; reinstatement requires all outstanding returns, service fees, and a solvency certificate in some cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Updating Declaration (Declaration de mise a jour annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the enterprise's registration in the Quebec Enterprise Register; changes (e.g., director changes, share transfers) must additionally be reported within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an administrative penalty of CAD 300; failure for two consecutive years allows the Registraire to strike off and dissolve the legal person d'office; restoration via REQ is costly and discretionary.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end -> June 30 deadline).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% for each full month of delay (maximum 12 months); repeated non-filing carries an additional 10% penalty on late-filed amounts; CRA may also issue arbitrary assessments and pursue director liability.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.50% combined federal and Quebec corporate tax rate (Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%), before abatements and credits
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian federal small business deduction reduces federal rate to 9.0% on first CA$500,000 of active business income, plus Quebec SME reduced rate of 5.4% on eligible small business profits; refundable SR&ED tax credits (federal 15%–35%, Quebec 14%–28%), Quebec innovation and manufacturing credits, and the federal general tax reduction are available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically via CRA My Business Account, EFILE, or recognized tax software (EDI / XML schema).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than six months after the corporation’s fiscal year-end. Any unpaid balance is due within two months after the fiscal year-end (three months for qualified Canadian-controlled private corporations).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from all business sources, including export sales of medical diagnostic scanners, intercompany transactions, and investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident corporations report worldwide income. Non-resident corporations operating in Canada report only Canadian-source active business income and generally file under Part I with Schedule 91; Part XIII withholdings are separately reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible business expenses, including transfer pricing adjustments, cost of goods sold, wages, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must prorate deductible expenses attributable to Canadian business. Transfer-pricing adjustments must be added back where arm’s length remuneration was not used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions, capital cost allowance, and carried-forward non-capital losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents compute taxable income using the same rules, but only Canadian-source income is included. Losses from foreign operations are generally excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal basic tax before investment tax credits and other non-refundable credit offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations claim treaty-based credits only if applicable; otherwise, the prorated federal tax applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month, capped at 12 months; a repeat penalty of 10% may apply. Additional daily fines and imprisonment can be imposed on summary conviction for failure to file a T2 return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec: Corporation Income Tax Return CO-17 filed via Revenu Quebec’s ‘CLICK – Entreprises’ electronic filing portal, EDI, or approved authorized software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within six months of the fiscal year-end. Quebec instalments are payable quarterly or monthly in accordance with Revenu Quebec’s instalment reminders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from business and property, including revenue from portable phased-array diagnostic scanner manufacturing and export sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Quebec through a permanent establishment reports Quebec-source income. A separate return must be filed for Quebec, with allocation factors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses, with a requirement to identify related-party transaction amounts and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must deduct only expenses reasonably attributable to Quebec income, and document transfer pricing for cross-border transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryovers and statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations include taxable Canadian income apportioned to Quebec, and may claim applicable Quebec deductions and tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec income tax before tax credits; the slider applies the general corporate rate and the reduced SME rate where eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are entitled to Quebec investment tax credits only if they maintain a qualified permanent establishment in Quebec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 0.5% per month, capped at 12 months, plus daily interest; a false omission penalty is 10% of the shortfall; criminal evasion penalties can reach 24 months’ imprisonment and fines up to CA$10,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid or deemed to be paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must provide an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by its home tax authority (e.g., U.S. Form 6166). The Canadian payer submits CRA Form NR301 (or NR302/NR303 for treaty-protected interest/royalties) to the International Tax Services Office. Once CRA certifies the non-resident’s treaty status, the reduced withholding rate is applied or refunded. For dividends to a U.S. parent company under Canada–U.S. DTA, the rate is 5% if the beneficial owner holds at least 10% of the voting shares and meets limitation on benefits; otherwise 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: interest 25%, royalties 25%. Under Canada–U.S. DTA: arm’s-length interest 10%, royalties 10% (0% for some copyright payments); under Canada–France, Canada–Germany, Canada–UK DTAs the treaty rate for patent or industrial royalties is generally 10%; interest is typically 10%; many modern DTAs provide 0% on arm’s-length interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation is required under CRA Information Circular IC 89-16R where the aggregate fair market value of reportable cross-border non-arm’s-length transactions exceeds CA$1,000,000 per year (goods) or CA$2,000,000 per year (services, interest, royalties); a Master File is additionally expected for multinational groups with consolidated gross revenue of CA$500,000,000 or more. Form T106 (Information Return of Non-Arm’s Length Transactions with Non-Residents) must be filed annually if the CA$1,000,000 threshold is exceeded.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain standalone Economic Substance Regulations of the type found in offshore centres. However, economic substance is required to obtain treaty benefits, avoid General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) recharacterization under s.245 of the Income Tax Act, and qualify as resident for Canadian tax purposes. A Quebec shell company with minimal staff, no physical operational presence, and no substantive management in Canada will be denied treaty relief and may be subject to GAAR adjustment, transfer-pricing penalties, and in severe cases criminal fraud prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Canadian-source revenue from the Quebec medical imaging exporter, using fabricated invoices, hiding assets in foreign trading vehicles, or intentionally misstating cost of goods sold to suppress taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.239: summary conviction — fine equal to 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 2 years; indictment — fine up to 2 times the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2): 50% of the understated tax plus interest. Quebec Taxation Act imposes equivalent fines and imprisonment up to 24 months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted withheld amounts under s.227.1 of the Income Tax Act and s.31.7 of the Quebec Taxation Act. Criminal conviction triggers personal restitution orders, travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment. The CRA may assess directors personally without first exhausting corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure / GAAR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An entity organized merely as a billing intermediary with no employees, office, contracts, or operational substance, or a structure that routes export profits through a zero-tax jurisdiction while the real management and economic activity take place in Quebec/Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under GAAR, CRA can disregard abusive transactions and reassess income attributable to the Canadian operating company. The misuse penalty under s.163(2) applies, and transfer-pricing adjustments attract a 10% penalty when the adjustment exceeds CA$5,000,000 or 10% of gross revenue. Fraud charges can be brought under the Criminal Code for intentional restructuring to evade tax, with penalties including fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers who authorize sham arrangements are jointly liable for the resulting tax shortfall. Courts may pierce the corporate veil for fraud; director travel bans and extradition for tax fraud are available where evasion exceeds relevant thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report an electronic wire transfer or SWIFT LC remittance of CA$10,000 or more within 24 hours; ignoring linked transaction requirements; failing to maintain beneficial-ownership records; issuing invoices to clients without proper KYC/AML screening, or using procurement agents in high-risk jurisdictions for ultrasound console component orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: administrative monetary penalties up to CA$200,000 for a corporation for non-compliance; repeat or willful violations upward of CA$1,000,000; criminal indictment for knowingly failing to disclose suspicious transactions can result in imprisonment up to 5 years and fines of up to CA$100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally fined up to CA$100,000 and imprisoned up to 6 months on summary conviction, or up to 5 years on indictment. FINTRAC and law enforcement may impose conditions, seek civil freezing orders, and travel bans against the responsible officers where money laundering through trade-based conduits is detected.
